analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials 10.12.26 10.16.26 Weekend Edition
key_insights: Industrials fell almost 90bps last week and materials rose nearly 300bps, both outperforming broader markets that were down 200bps. Elevated commodity prices tied to geopolitical concerns are cited as a direct corollary to materials strength.

Continued weakness in the AI/data center complex came with defensives rising on an absolute basis, specifically defense and waste. Leverage and SMID names continue to underperform meaningfully, and the VIX spiked, with quality the dominant factor. The desk reads this as uncertainty accelerating.

About 1/3 of industrials and materials companies report this week. Asia and Europe read-throughs: strength in VACN SW orders, SU FP raising organic growth and margin guidance for the year, Yaskawa order strength, DHL GR beat and raise with strength in peak season ahead, and GIVN SW strength.

Prime book: US equities were net sold on the week (-0.9 SDs 1-year). Single stocks saw the largest net selling in 8 weeks (-1.2 SDs), with long and short sales at 1.5 to 1. Macro products were marginally net sold (-0.1 SDs), driven by risk unwinds.

8 of 11 sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by Info Tech, Consumer Disc, Industrials and Financials. Health Care, Comm Svcs and Staples were net bought, which the desk describes as an incrementally defensive posture.

Info Tech was the worst performing US and global sector and the most net sold (-1.6 SDs 1-year), with long sales to short sales at 6 to 1. All subsectors were net sold. Semis & Semi Equip made up 57% of Info Tech net selling and now make up 9.5% of total US net MV on the Prime book (39th percentile vs 1 year, 88th vs 5 years).
US-listed ETF shorts decreased 1.9% (1.5% month/month), driven by covering in Small Cap and Credit ETFs, partly offset by shorting in Financials and Large Cap Equity ETFs.

GE reports Tue 10/20 pre-market with a 5% implied move. The stock is down three quarters in a row and four of the last five. EV/EBITDA has fallen from 35x to 28x and P/E from 45x to 36x. The desk says the difference from March/April is that the conflict is now six months old with no end in sight, which could change maintenance decisions. Upside sources: higher 2028 guidance, growth durability commentary, orders reaccelerating after a Q3 slowdown.

GM reports Tue 10/20 with a 5% implied move and the stock up four quarters in a row. GM has not missed headline earnings since Q2 2022 or EBIT since Q4 2023. It is one of the few well-owned autos names. The desk expects more of the same in Q3 and early 2027 commentary.

MMM reports Tue 10/20 with a 5% implied move. Expectations for organic growth are around 4%, versus 5% in Q2, and the company said organic would slow in the back half. The stock has given up all of its earnings gains and trades at 17x EPS and 12x EV/EBITDA. The desk thinks positioning skews net negative.

NOC reports Tue 10/20 with a 5% implied move. The stock is down two quarters in a row, three of four and four of six. Concerns are free cash flow and the recent FAXX contract loss. Shares short are at highs and nearly 2x a year ago, but low versus float and liquidity. Valuation is 17x earnings and 13x EV/EBITDA.

RTX reports Tue 10/20 with a 4% implied move. The stock was up 7% on Q2 and has been 50/50 on earnings recently. Short interest is low at 13.6mm shares. Focus: organic growth, Pratt margins, AOG trajectory and the munition framework agreement update.

CSX reports Wed 10/21 after market with a 4% implied move. The stock is up six quarters in a row. Short interest is at highs at 43mm shares versus 25mm a year ago (4 days to cover, 2% of float). Deal odds for UNP NSC have come in, and investors debate whether CSX carries an M&A premium.

PKG reports Wed 10/21 post market with a 4% implied move. Containerboard is one of few crowded areas in paper & packaging, with PKG at the top, followed by SW and IP. Valuation is 17x earnings and 10x EV/EBITDA, shares short are at lows, and the stock is rangebound $210-250, holding the 200-day, with a breakout above $240 on a better update.

TSLA reports Wed 10/21 post market with a 6% implied move. The stock is down three quarters in a row and four of the last five. Q3 delivery data was better. The desk expects flattish non-GAAP gross margins. Essentially all top shareholders added last quarter, and short interest is range bound at low levels.

URI reports Wed 10/21 post market with a 7% implied move after squeezes of 10% (Q1'26) and 23% (Q2'26). The desk calls it arguably the most crowded long in machinery. Short interest fell 1.4mm shares to 2.6 days to cover (2% of float). Focus: end market commentary, rental rates and redistribution costs.

WCN reports Wed 10/21 post market with no options implied move. Focus is on landfill issues: remediation at the Chiquita landfill after California law AB 28, and a potential elevated temperature event at the Avena landfill. Short interest is at 4mm shares, the highest in a decade. Valuations are depressed versus history.
